newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH CROWN TRADING NERVOUS AFTER TRADE FIGURES.
newsitem.headline: CZECH CROWN TRADING NERVOUS AFTER TRADE FIGURES.

text.p: The Czech crown traded nervously on Monday morning after the Czech Statistical Office said the 1996 trade deficit widened to a record 160.3 billion crowns ($5.8 billion) from a 95.7-billion crown deficit in 1995.

The crown dipped to around 27.888 against the dollar and 17.057 against the mark, implying +4.07 percent against its mark/dollar basket mid-point immediately after the figures were released. Then, it recovered to around +4.2 percent but remained jittery.
"It's quite nervous, spreads are wide...(but) bad figures were expected, and the figures are not seasonally adjusted," said Petr Tomek of Zivnostenska Banka.
